newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures failed to recover from a weak start and despite finding solid support, a Spanish franc bond issue and comments from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan kept the contract under pressure.

The June contract suffered soon after the open from domestic and non-resident sales alike, inspired by caution ahead of a series of U.S. figures and the Greenspan address, but bounced off support below 127.30.
Although the contract struggled higher, a wave of supply from the French Treasury, a German bank and then Spain ensured any gains were limited.
The contract settled down 0.58 at 127.32 after touching the day's low just prior to the close after Greenspan's comments.
"The fall was a simple reaction to covering and the remarks of the Fed chairman," a trader said. He said he expected support at 127.28/30 to hold.

While traders said the Treasury auction of 22.5 billion francs of two- and five-year BTANs had gone reasonably well, they said the four billion 15-year franc issue from Spain had weighed on the market.
One trader said a French brokerage hit the contract by hedging soon after the issue, lead managed by Banque Paribas.
"It was expensive and the placement did not go too well," the trader said.
Traders also said the relatively high bid-to-cover ratio at the Treasury's BTAN sale had been boosted by a number of large bids at unrealistically low prices.
The June futures contract recovered, however, on GLOBEX trade and was testing a gap left at the open above 127.54.

Traders said the market remained nervous and opinons were divided as to whether the recent rise in yields would tempt investors back into the market or whether they would wait for the Fed's policy council meeting on March 25.
The franc was little changed against the mark.

It traded within a tight range between 3.3750 and 3.3734. It fell sharply against the dollar, however, after the Greenspan comments, which some interpreted as pointing to a rise in U.S. short term interest rates next week.
The franc fell as low as 5.7045 from the day's high of 5.6387.
As expected the Bank of France left the intervention rate unchanged at Thursday's regular money market tender.
